journey.title: Tab away after typing an unavailable delivery date
journey.goal: Leaving the date field with Tab closes the calendar even when the typed date is outside the delivery window

steps.title: Type a date outside the delivery window

functionalJourney.title: Move the delivery into June with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking through the calendar to June and choosing a day fills the delivery date

guards.title: Type a valid delivery date and Tab away
guards.goal: A correctly typed date is committed and the calendar closes when the user tabs away

plan.root_cause: The datepicker remains open when focus leaves the input field via Tab because there is no blur event listener to hide the picker; it only hides on mousedown outside the picker.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field in the Datepicker constructor (non‑inline mode) that calls this.hide() to close the picker when the input loses focus.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now close the datepicker when moving focus away with Tab, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.4.3 Focus Order.
functional_risks: Potential premature hiding if focus temporarily leaves the input while interacting with the datepicker popup via keyboard (e.g., arrow navigation).
Inline datepickers are unaffected because the listener is added only in the non‑inline branch.
verification_requirements: After typing a date and pressing Tab, the datepicker must close.
Selecting a date via mouse or keyboard within the popup should still work and close appropriately.
Opening the datepicker via focus must still show the picker.
Inline datepickers should continue to behave as before.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker remains open when focus leaves the input field via Tab because there is no blur event listener to hide the picker; it only hides on mousedown outside the picker. Previous attempts added a blur listener but caused premature hiding when clicking inside the picker because blur fires before the click event.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field in the non-inline branch that calls this.hide() only when the user is not interacting with the picker. Set a flag on mousedown on the picker element to ignore the blur for a brief moment, allowing click events to process before hiding.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now close the datepicker when moving focus away with Tab, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.4.3 Focus Order. The picker also closes when focus leaves the input for any reason, unless the user is clicking inside the picker.
functional_risks: If the user clicks inside the picker, the mousedown flag prevents hiding, but the picker will still hide on subsequent blur if focus leaves the input. This is acceptable because the click will have been processed.
The setTimeout with 0 delay relies on the event loop; in rare cases the click might not process in time, but the risk is low.
verification_requirements: After typing a date and pressing Tab, the datepicker must close.
Selecting a date via mouse or keyboard within the popup should still work and not close prematurely.
Opening the datepicker via focus must still show the picker.
Inline datepickers should continue to behave as before.
